newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Oct 10.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- MING PAO -- The Hang Seng Index set a new record on Wednesday, closing at 12,250.57. Market analyists remained optimistic on the near future.
-- Former judge Arthur Garcia is considering pulling out of the race for 1997 Chief Executive because of lack of support from Beijing.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY -- Staff of China Motor Bus said they will go ahead with a planned strike next Tuesday and Wednesday if they fail to get an agreement from their employer on pensions.
-- A sculptor who vandalised a statue of Queen Victoria was jailed for 28 days.
-- APPLE DAILY -- Twenty Diaoyu (Senkaku) islands activists stormed into the Japanese Consulate and stayed for half an hour. Governor Chris Patten said the incident was very serious.
-- Beijing-funded WEN WEI PO -- Chinese Premier Li Peng said administrative reforms would improve the quality of civil servants and raise efficiency.
-- Chinese and overseas experts expressed optimism towards Chinese agriculture's potential, believing it would not form a threat to world grain markets.
-- SING TAO -- Fighter planes of China's Nanjing Military District overflew the disputed Diaoyu (Senkaku) islands last month to show Japan China's determination to guard its sovereignty.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- A real estate company of the Shanghai municipal government was planned to buy into Hong Kong's Knight Frank property company.

-- English-language SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- The myth that Hong Kong hotels are fully booked for the 1997 handover period has been shattered. Hong Kong Hotels Association chairman Thomas Axmacher said up to 30 per cent of rooms were vacant.
-- Bank of China Group Securities is seeking to futher expand by courting more institutional clients and developing its merchant banking business.
-- English-language HONGKONG STANDARD -- U.S. Customs is expected to stage another 30-day monitoring in Hong Kong in connection with a long-running dispute over textile exports.
